briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Turns Political Weapon as Feds Push Psilocybin and Rescheduling Toward the Finish Line
briefs.top: In Michigan, the 24% wholesale tax is now a genuine campaign issue with both parties' energy aimed at repeal, while operators keep opening doors and cutting deals despite the squeeze. Nationally, momentum keeps building — DEA's rescheduling hearing has wrapped and awaits a ruling, mega-M&A is reshaping the MSO landscape, and Compass Pathways is racing toward what could be the first FDA-approved psilocybin therapy.

local.text: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is actively courting cannabis industry donors while pledging to kill or gut the 24% wholesale tax, a sign operators now have real leverage in this fall's governor's race.

The wholesale tax is generating a fraction of projections — about $37M in Q2 versus a $105M target — evidence the industry's lawsuits and repeal push are gaining real ammunition ahead of the case heading to trial.

Fields Cannary's hospitality-driven dispensary-restaurant concept in Muskegon is still moving forward toward a fall opening, proof that ambitious retail buildouts remain viable even under tax pressure.

Jars Cannabis resolved its long-running Flock surveillance camera dispute with Madison Heights, clearing the way for smoother operations at the store that opened after the city initially denied its license.
The federal hemp THC ban was pushed back from Nov. 12 to Dec. 11 after President Trump signed a delay bill, giving Michigan hemp-adjacent retailers extra runway while Congress writes permanent rules.

national.text: DEA's formal hearings on rescheduling marijuana to Schedule III have concluded, with a ruling now pending — a step that could unlock standard business tax deductions and fuel further consolidation industry-wide.

Curaleaf formally launched its $4-per-share takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis, creating a combined platform with pro forma revenue exceeding $1.5 billion — the clearest signal yet that major MSOs are betting big on cross-border scale.

Compass Pathways' COMP360 psilocybin therapy for treatment-resistant depression earned the FDA's Commissioner's National Priority Voucher and a rolling NDA review, putting it on track to become the first approved psilocybin drug as soon as late 2026 or early 2027.

The FDA finalized its clinical trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and set a September 14 public hearing on psychedelic therapeutics, which analysts say signals a friendlier regulatory path for Compass, Atai, Cybin and GH Research.

DEA is now sending detailed rescheduling-protection questionnaires to state-licensed medical cannabis businesses in Colorado, an early but concrete sign the agency is building the compliance framework operators will need under Schedule III.
